axisE_cdar_full_sample_calibration_check.interpretation: CDaR L is a SINGLE constant fit on the entire realized sample by explicit design (documented in ctaB_pipeline.py's apply_leverage_cdar docstring); a shock placed near the END of the sample changes the constant applied to EVERY day including the very first day of the backtest. This is not a per-day causality bug (there is no such notion for a single full-sample scalar) but it IS a real in-sample/retrospective-calibration property: the realized 0.9718x leverage was chosen WITH HINDSIGHT of the entire 8.17-year realized path, including 2025-2026 data. A live/paper deployment could not have known this constant in Jan 2018; it would have had to re-estimate CDaR on a trailing/expanding window, which was NOT done here or in Stage A. This is disclosed in the docstring but not flagged as a limitation in CTA_PREREG.md or the pipeline's own adoption-gate reporting.
